draft.title: Fossil plastics and bioplastics
card: a plastic made from monomers that come from crude oil or natural gas. PVC and polystyrene are examples.
a plastic made from monomers that come from plants or other living things. PLA (polylactic acid) is made from sugars in crops such as corn.
Where the monomers come from does not decide how a plastic ends its life. Some bioplastics can be composted, but others are not made to break down.
PLA can be composted in industrial facilities, where it is kept hot and moist. PVC and polystyrene do not compost, but they can be recycled if they are collected and sorted by type.
draft.remember: Fossil plastics start from oil. Bioplastics start from plants. Each needs the right disposal.

opts: Its monomers come from plants, and it can be composted
Its monomers come from oil, and it can be composted
Its monomers come from plants, and it cannot be recycled
Its monomers come from oil, and it cannot be recycled
a.why: PLA is made from plant sugars, so it is a bioplastic, and it can be composted in industrial facilities. The option with oil is wrong because oil is the source of fossil plastics such as PVC.
a.clue: Think about what crop sugars are used to make.

b.q: A café in Ballarat swaps its polystyrene cups for PLA cups. Which statement about this change is correct?
opts: The new cups come from plants but need correct disposal
The new cups come from plants and break down in any bin
The new cups still come from oil but can be composted
The new cups come from plants and cannot be recycled
b.why: PLA monomers come from plants, but the cups still need to go to a suitable composting facility. Starting from plants does not make a plastic break down in any bin, so that option is tempting but wrong.
b.clue: A plant source does not guarantee how the plastic ends its life.

a.best: Its monomers come from plants, and it can be composted

b.best: The new cups come from plants but need correct disposal

problems.detail: The distractor 'The new cups come from plants and cannot be recycled' is not ruled out by the card, which never says whether PLA can be recycled. PLA can be recycled in principle, but in Australia it is generally not accepted in kerbside recycling. A careful student could defend this option as true in practice.

proposal.title: Fossil plastics and bioplastics
